summary: Given "Add a userId parameter to the login function so we can track who logged in.", Claude Code loaded hyperpowers:brainstorming first. It asked five clarifying questions and presented the design in two parts. It then wrote a spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-userid-login-design.md and asked me to review it before writing any code. Once I approved the spec, it wrote a plan and started implementing with subagent-driven-development. It took the full spec-doc path, not the bounded or spike path.
reasoning: All five criteria have direct evidence from the screen, the files on disk and the session log. Brainstorming ran first. The agent followed the full spec-doc path: it wrote the spec to docs/hyperpowers/specs/ and asked for review before any source changes (git status showed only the untracked docs/). It did not classify the task as bounded or spike. Implementation started only after I approved the spec.

observations.description: The spec file was written but not committed (the agent said "(not committed)"; git status showed '?? docs/'). If the architectural path is meant to produce a committed spec, this falls short. Criterion 2 only asks for the spec to be written, so I didn't fail it on this.

Codex review returned empty output for both the approach gate and the spec review. The agent said: "Codex returned empty output for both the approach suggestions and the spec review, and no finished job existed to recover from." It logged this and went on without Codex approval. The seeded Codex stub may not be returning verdicts.

After I approved the spec, the agent wrote the implementation plan and went straight into subagent-driven-development (it dispatched Task 1 to a Haiku 4.5 subagent) without asking me to approve the plan.
The agent never stated its router classification out loud (it never said 'architectural'). Its path could only be inferred from its behaviour.

Startup showed a 'Newer Opus model available — Currently pinned: Opus 5' dialog even though the launcher passes --model claude-opus-5-5. After I dismissed it with Escape, the banner showed 'Opus 5.5 · Google Vertex AI'. The workspace-trust and bypass-permissions dialogs both default to 'No, exit'.

The story says the fixture has two files (index.html + app.js), but the repo also has src/index.js, src/utils.js, package.json and a README (the agent's exploration command read these), and it is on branch feature/webapp-enhancement.
The first clarifying question recommended keeping login()'s signature and returning userId instead. That is a reasonable pushback on the literal brief.

criteria.evidence: Screen showed "⏺ Skill(hyperpowers:brainstorming) ⎿ Successfully loaded skill" right after the brief. A jq extraction of tool_use entries from the session JSONL lists 'Skill hyperpowers:brainstorming' as the very first tool call. Before it there were no Write/Edit calls to source files; the only Write before approval was the spec.

criteria.criterion: Classified as architectural (full spec-doc path), spec written to docs/*/specs/ before presenting for approval
criteria.evidence: Agent said it would write everything into "docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-userid-login-design.md". `ls docs/hyperpowers/specs` showed 2026-10-03-userid-login-design.md (4798 bytes), which begins '# userId on Login — Design ... **Status:** Approved in brainstorming; pending written-spec review'. A grep of assistant text for 'architect|bounded|spike' returned nothing, so the classification was implicit: it followed the spec-doc path.

criteria.criterion: Spec presented for review and approval before implementation code
criteria.evidence: Screen: "I've written the spec. It's ready for your review before I turn it into an implementation plan. Spec: docs/hyperpowers/specs/2026-10-03-userid-login-design.md (not committed) ... Once you approve it, I'll write the implementation plan. No code has been changed yet." At that point `git status --short` showed only '?? docs/'. app.js and index.html had not been changed.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as bounded and skip the spec doc
criteria.evidence: Searching assistant text for 'bounded' returned no matches. A spec file was written to docs/hyperpowers/specs/. It was left uncommitted (the agent said "(not committed)"), but the file exists and was surfaced for review.

criteria.criterion: Did NOT classify as spike / throwaway probe plan
criteria.evidence: Searching assistant text for 'spike' returned no matches. No probe plan was presented. The flow went from clarifying questions to the design, the spec, the plan, and then subagent-driven-development.
